Consonantal i

Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

night noun

also nights, at night, by night, at this time of night, at this hour of the night, during the night, while it is still night

classical

Mart. 2.90.10: sit nox cum somnō
Traupman 88
Traupman 88: at this time of night, hōc noctis

nox, noctis f.

noun, third declension

At night is noctū or nocte; late at night, multā nocte (see late at night); last night, proximā nocte (see last night); at this time of night, hōc noctis (Traupman 88).

Other words

  • noctū — at night, by night

    adverb · also used · classical · Gell. 17.10.11: interdius fūmāre Aetnam, noctū flammigāre; Cic. Fam. 9.2.1: cōnscrīpsī epistulam noctū

    The opposite of interdiū, by day.

  • dē nocte — during the night, while it is still night

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.3.4: in comitium … dē nocte vēnit, in the night (Lewis & Short s.v. dē); Hor. Ep. 1.2.32: ut jugulent hominēs, surgunt dē nocte latrōnēs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 351: by night, noctū, dē nocte

    Of what is done in the night hours, often before dawn, as robbers get up in the night. Traupman 86 also gives it for “after dark” and “in the dark”, which it does not mean (see after dark, darkness).

Examples

  • sit nox cum somnō, sit sine līte diēs

    let the night have sleep, and the day no quarrelsMart. 2.90.10

  • nox ubi jam media est somnōque silentia praebet, et canis et variae conticuistis avēs

    when it is midnight and the night offers silence for sleep, you too fall silent, dog, and you, many-coloured birdsOv. Fast. 5.429–430

  • quis hic est homō, quem ante aedīs videō hōc noctis?

    who is this man I see in front of the house at this time of night?Plaut. Amph. 1.1.136 (Lewis & Short s.v. hic)

See also day, good night, tonight, last night, every night, late at night, midnight, day and night, after dark.
